elements.name: Path of the Giant
elements.desc: Barbarians who walk the Path of the Giant draw strength from the same primal forces as giants. As they rage, these barbarians surge with elemental power and grow in size, taking on forms that evoke the glory of giants. Some might be descended from giants, while others might have been raised among them or had their latent giant blood awakened by a moment of extreme trauma or triumph.

elements.name: Giant's Power
elements.desc:
3rd-level Path of the Giant feature.

You learn how to imbue yourself with the immense strength of giants. As a bonus action, you can enter a state of giant's power for 1 minute. While in this state, you gain the following benefits:

Size. If you are smaller than Large, you become Large, along with anything you are wearing. If you lack the room to become Large, your size doesn't change.
Reach. Your reach increases by 5 feet.
Elemental Strike. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon or an unarmed strike, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to the target. The damage type is your choice of acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

elements.name: Giant's Havoc
elements.desc:
3rd-level Path of the Giant feature.

Your primal connection to giants manifests in a variety of ways. You gain the following benefits:

Druidcraft. You learn the Druidcraft cantrip, which doesn't count against the number of barbarian cantrips you know. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for this cantrip.
Powerful Build. You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

elements.name: Elemental Cleaver
elements.desc:
6th-level Path of the Giant feature.

Your rage infuses your weapons with elemental energy. When you enter your rage, you can choose one weapon you are holding and infuse it with one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder. For the duration of your rage, the weapon deals an extra 1d6 damage of the chosen type on a hit, and its damage is considered magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

If you drop or throw the weapon, it returns to your hand at the end of your turn.

elements.name: Mighty Impel
elements.desc:
10th-level Path of the Giant feature.

You can hurl creatures through the air with tremendous force. As an action, you can attempt to throw a creature you can see within 30 feet of you that is no more than one size larger than you. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be moved up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. If the target is moved into a solid object or another creature, it takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage and falls prone.

elements.name: Demiurgic Colossus
elements.desc:
14th-level Path of the Giant feature.

Your connection to giants allows you to become a truly colossal force of nature. While you are in your giant's power state, you gain the following benefits:

Colossal Size. Your size can increase to Huge, along with anything you are wearing. If you lack the room to become Huge, your size doesn't change.
Colossal Reach. Your reach increases by an additional 5 feet (for a total of 10 feet while in this state).
Colossal Strike. The extra damage of your Elemental Strike increases to 1d8.
